name: Temples of the Deep South
theme: A pilgrimage across the far south of Tamil Nadu — from the island of Rameswaram, through Madurai and the Tirunelveli country, to the land's end at Kanyakumari
region: Far southern Tamil Nadu (Ramanathapuram to Kanyakumari)
description: The far south of Tamil Nadu narrows to a point where three seas meet, and along the way it holds some of the most distinctive temples in the land. This circuit follows the old pilgrim road to the land's end. It begins at Rameswaram, the island shrine of Ramanathaswamy with its immense corridors, where Rama is said to have worshipped Shiva, and turns inland to Madurai, where the fish-eyed goddess Meenakshi reigns in her great temple. In the Tirunelveli country stand Nellaiappar, whose pillars ring with music; Sankarankovil, where Shiva and Vishnu share one shrine as Sankaranarayanar; and Thiruchendur, where Murugan faces the waves. Courtallam's Kutralanathar rises beside cascading falls at the foot of the Western Ghats. Then come Suchindram, where Shiva, Vishnu and Brahma share a single lingam; Thiruvattar, where Vishnu reclines as Adikesava between two rivers; and finally Kanyakumari, where the virgin goddess keeps watch over the meeting of the Bay of Bengal, the Arabian Sea and the Indian Ocean.
